rfam.comment: The mammalian CPEB3 ribozyme is a self cleaving RNA located in the second intron of the CPEB3 gene which belongs to a family of genes regulating messenger RNA polyadenylation [1]. This ribozyme is highly conserved and found only in mammals [1]. The CPEB3 ribozyme is structurally and biochemically related to the human hepatitis delta virus (HDV) ribozyme (Rfam:RF00094) and the HDV ribozyme is proposed to have arisen from the human transcriptome [1]. There is currently only one other known self cleaving ribozyme in mammals, the CoTC motif (Rfam:RF00621)[2]. The structure of CPEB3 ribozyme has been reported in PDB 7QR3.
